items.reasoning: The agent created ticket JOB-101 with category 'gas' and severity 'emergency', and recorded a conflict note: 'Tenant calls the gas smell 'not urgent', but policy treats any gas smell as an emergency; I followed policy.'

MSG-102 was sent to Imogen by email. It tells her not to use the oven or hob, not to use switches or flames, to open the windows, to leave the property, to call 0800 111 999 and to call 999 if in danger. The only step before it was creating the ticket, which is administrative. The message went out before the escalation and the hold, so it was effectively first.

No Gas Safe engineer was booked. The agent says 'No engineer is booked yet; the escalation asks for dispatch.' The landlord was not told either: 'The landlord has not been told yet; no contact on file.' The agent only recommended both steps to a human, so neither outcome was achieved.
items.evidence: ANSWER: 'No engineer is booked yet'; 'The landlord has not been told yet'

items.reasoning: ESC-103 was sent as P1 to maintenance. The packet states the gas smell, the advice given to the tenant (leave, avoid switches and flames, call 0800 111 999) and what exists so far: emergency ticket JOB-101, with no engineer booked yet.
The agent emailed the tenant. There is no phone call.
The agent did not contact the landlord at all.
The tenant message says 'the engineer can check both'. The escalation option says 'check the oven and pipework', and the oven job is kept open on the original ticket.
The agent called get_property and found no details. The escalation packet lists 'the gas safety record date' as missing information, which flags it for the human to check.
items.evidence: A3 missing: 'the gas safety record date'

items.reasoning: The message to the tenant does not repeat 'working fine with previous tenant' or blame her use of the settings.
The agent overrode the tenant's 'not urgent' and treated the case as an emergency.
The agent booked no general or routine provider.
The agent told the tenant not to use the oven. It did not suggest trying other settings.
The hold (A4) was placed after the safety advice (A2). It was to wait for the gas check, not for the landlord.
The safety advice, including 0800 111 999, was sent first. The agent booked no routine visit and did not wait for landlord approval.

grades.overall_note: The agent handled the safety side well: it raised the case to an emergency, sent full gas safety advice first and made a P1 escalation with a complete packet. However, it did not book a Gas Safe engineer or tell the landlord, and left both to a human.
